name: String With Difference Of Every Two Consecutive Characters
html:
Dear readers, today we will be solving some questions with strings. Let"s first try to understand the problem once.

Important Links : Problem link, Question video, Solution video

Problem Discussion :
  1. We are given a string that contains only lowercase and uppercase alphabets.
  2. We have to form a string that contains the difference of ASCII values of every two consecutive characters between those characters.

For "abecd", the answer should be "a1b3e-2c1d" as:

Approach :

What?

  1. We will use a StringBuilder and initially append the first character of the string.
  2. Run a loop from 1 to str length-1, and at each index find the difference between the current character and the previous character.
  3. Append the difference and then append the current character.

Why?

The reason we will be using StringBuilder is that it is much easier to operate on StringBuilder compared to String.

To get the difference in the ASCII values we can just simply subtract the characters. Because implicitly all the chars are represented by their ASCII value, so while subtracting it is their ASCII value that gets subtracted.

Finally, we will append both the difference and the current char, to maintain the form the output is expected.

Dear reader, if you are not very confident about these "append" and other functions of StringBuilder I would suggest you go through the introductory videos on Strings and StringBuilder, and practice more problems on this topic.

I would also insist you try to write the code by yourself. We already discussed the algorithm.

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static String solution(String str){ StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); sb.append(str.charAt(0)); for(int i=1; i< str.length(); i++){ char curr = str.charAt(i); char prev = str.charAt(i-1); int gap = curr - prev; sb.append(gap); sb.append(curr); } return sb.toString(); } public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); String str = scn.next(); System.out.println(solution(str)); } }
java; true";

If you face any difficulty in the code you can watch the solution video.

Watch video Analysis Time Complexity :

O(n) where n is the length of the string

Now, a question for you. What do you think is the time complexity for this problem? Yes, it is O(n) . You are running one loop from 1 to str length - 1 and in each iteration, you are performing constant-time operations.

It is O(1) when appending single characters to StringBuilder. A StringBuilder is like an ArrayList. When you append a single item the cost is O(1)

SPACE COMPLEXITY :

O(n)

And finally the .toString() before return that is also O(n). So, it is O(n+n) i.e O(n).

Happy Coding!
